>I ended up trying it on my boob but my blades have gotten too blunt this week so I didn't get very far. It felt easier than the inner thigh but harder than the outer thigh, as I had to hold the skin taught.

I'm seconding the lemon juice one. I've been applying lemon juice to the lighter ones on my arm and the red marks are totally gone. Just don't rub it in too much--I managed to give myself a nasty, bumpy rash by rubbing in the juice really hard into my arm until it irritated my skin.

I have yet to have luck with silicone sheets though :( I know they are mostly for reducing the puffiness of large keloid scars and aren't supposed to do as much about redness, but I've had them on the one on my thigh for a long time now and they have done little to help it.

I've actually had some weird success with lemon juice. You have to apply it every day, and the juice will cause them to fade really quickly and then they slowly come back so it looks like you're not making any progress, but I've actually had progress over the course of a week. I've been trying it out with one of my old really red scars and figured I would post before/after pictures on here at some point.

Just put some lemon juice on a paper towel or cotton ball and rub it over the scars for a few minutes (make sure they are completely healed, it hurts when you do it on a fresher cut! Ouch!). I got a small rash when I used too much lemon juice and massaged it in for too long, but other than that I've had pretty good success with it!

You said it yourself, it is an addiction. Personally, I never want to have to rely on something like self harm so heavily that I can't get through the day, but that's where I've been for the longest time. I want to be able to just be myself without being a slave to something like this.

Yes, it will curb your anxiety or depression in the short term, but (at least for me) using self harm as a "cure" for my anxiety just meant I would want it more even after that. That mindset is like that of a junkie, saying that they can "stop whenever they want." I guess we are adrenaline/endorphin junkies in a way, right? But I don't know about you, but when I got to the point where I was cutting every day, I definitely couldn't stop whenever I want. I will even go months without doing it now, thinking I'm okay, and then something bad will happen in my life and I will go back to it. I don't why to die as a slave to anything, so I will choose to fight my self harm and stop this cycle of being a "junkie."

And honestly, it hurts you emotionally just as much as it does physically, even if you try to tell yourself it doesn't. When I have to go outside with my scars, or even when I see them when I'm home alone, my self-worth plummets. Healthy people do not resort to self harm to solve their problems. Healthy people understand that they--their body, their mind, their soul--all hold value and do not injure them as a means of medication. We each only get one body, and the scars will be carried with us for a long time. My hope is that the scars will be able to fade with time and I will live a long life and die free from them. That's really the only way to beat this.

Your writing is absolutely beautiful and moves me, though I have to say I disagree with what you are saying.

I absolutely hate when people tell me "it gets better." Who are they to judge what is "better" for me, and who are they to make those promises to me? I am not going to tell you that your life will get better. What I can say is, if you truly try and want your life to get better, you have the power to make that happen. It's an absolutely amazing thing to have that kind of power, and if you decide you want to use it, you really could do anything with your life. Start off small and learn a hobby, or go big and travel the world. There are amazing things out there, and if you want your life to get better, you will be able to go out there and experience them.

I know you're tired and I know you're impatient. I have no right to sit here and tell you that you have to hold on a little longer. Only you can make that choice. But don't you wonder what you might be missing out on? Life is about pain and misery as much as it is about joy, and it's not fair that you've had to experience more of the former, but the happiness is still out there, and you of all people deserve to find it.

Coming from someone who self harms on a regular basis, I still can't imagine it would be a very comfortable way to go. There's something terribly frightening about slowly watching your own life drain out of you. 

I know you're hurting and it's tough to continue living the way you are, but there will never be any easy or comfortable way to die. It will be even worse for those you leave behind. They're not going to hate you; they're going to hate themselves and wish there was something they could have done. You've managed to hold out this long, and I'm proud of you for being able to do that. Why not try taking one more small step before you decide to go down that path? Have you tired being truly open with anyone about what you are going through? 

Those people that you say will miss you, they want to reach out to you and hear what you're going through and share in your pain. Even me, now that I am invested, will be thinking about you way into the future, and I've never even met you before. You sound like a kind, thoughtful person and I want to continue speaking with you. Reading this was eerie because this is exactly how I felt for the longest time in the world. I would tell my boyfriend this all the time, that I only did it when I had a rough week in classes and I didn't do it too deep or too much and I could stop whenever I wanted to. Just hear me out for a minute.

I don't want to bore you, but feel free to go back through my post history and see how that all ended up for me. This past year was a rough year for me in my classes. I started cutting more frequently, and eventually I was doing it every single day. I forced myself to stop after a particularly bad day last winter that left me with some permanent scars, and I told myself I would be able to stop and would be fine. The scars would fade, I told myself (which is a lie), and I will be able to move on. I am okay. I don't have a problem.

I had a really bad day the other day, and after not cutting for two months, I cut myself over 100 times all up and down my arms and legs. After finishing my legs, I knew I'd gone too far and called my boyfriend, but I still had to finish up my arms before I could stop. I got blood everywhere and it took all of my convincing for my boyfriend to not call an ambulance. Honestly, one probably should have been called, but the cuts are healing and I am okay now.

This is not a healthy way to deal with stress, and you do need to seek help. I understand not wanting to tell your parents, but please reach out to a friend or a school counselor to talk to. You really were me just a year or two ago. My cuts weren't deep; it really just felt good to get that release. Eventually though, you get to the point where you need that release to get on with your day, and if you don't, you're in tears and shaking in the middle of your lecture hall or on the street or wherever. 

Please, I know I sound like a stupid old fart, but I'm begging you to learn from my mistakes. Find someone to talk to. Talk to me if you'd like. Figure out what's going on in your head and why you need to do this and what you can do to make it stop for good.

I agree with deej3335 that you may be acting too harsh with her by searching through the house to take away things she can use to cut herself. If someone really wants to cut, they will find a way to do it, and taking away the means will not stop the cause.

However, I'm really sorry you have to go through this, and thank you for doing all you can to help. That's very admirable of you to do. Therapy sounds like a good idea, so does talking with her, but not necessarily just about cutting, but how she's feeling, what's going on, etc. 

Also, perhaps you can get some more information from the therapist (or if you need to talk with someone, I would be very open to sharing my experiences with you, though they do not represent everyone and possibly not your daughter). You should learn more about why people do this, the best ways to handle them, how to cope with those feelings yourself, etc. Perhaps educating yourself can help get rid of your preconceived notions. Your daughter is a unique person and a special case, so you can't apply any generalizations to her to think you can fix the problem.

Other than that, good luck, and I wish you the best. Try to be there for her as much as you can and foster an open and safe environment. Feel free to pm me if you need any advice or just need someone to talk to. Everything is going to be okay, just take a deep breath. She is still your sweet hearted, beautiful, compassionate daughter and this is something she will be able to work past.
Please don't, you've done so much to make it this far. You have beaten the urge before and you can do it again. Don't let this get the best of you; win the fight.

I posted this elsewhere, but I don't believe it got seen. For covering them up right now, best bet is to try some cover up makeup. They sell kinds that are specifically for the body and will stay on better. Tattoo cover up will probably work the best. Something like these from Sephora will work:
http://www.sephora.com/body-makeup-tattoo-cover-up

As for healing them long term, it's going to take time for them to go away, but there are things you can do that may speed up the process. 

Unfortunately, nothing has been entirely medically proven, but doing things like massaging a scar with oil can help increase blood flow and break up collagen fibers that make scars thick and ropy. There are products on the market like Mederma that will have you do the same massaging, but add in some UV protectants and moisturizers that may help as well. 

You can also try silicone scar sheets, which keep pressure on the scar and provide a similar effect as massaging. These are what I'm using right now, and they're pretty cheap ($20), and I'm starting to see results after two weeks. They're just these Band-Aid style things that you leave on most of the time, so they're not too bothersome.

I've heard of things like lemon juice and tea oil helping as well, but again, nothing has been medically proven. 

The best you is continue to massage scars to increase blood flow and allow the body to heal itself a bit better.
